content.text: Role in HD:

antipsychotics may partly suppress chorea and agitation; an alt first-line tx w depression; dose is ↑ until intolerable SE (eg, lethargy, parkinsonism) or Sx are controlled. clozapine: frequent WBC counts (agranulocytosis risk).
Risperidone (Risperdal) boxed warning:
Boxed: elderly pts w dementia-related psychosis on antipsychotics at ↑ risk of death; RISPERDAL not approved for dementia-related psychosis.
Risperidone (Risperdal) cerebrovascular risk in elderly dementia:
Cerebrovascular reactions (stroke, TIA), incl fatalities, in elderly pts w dementia-related psychosis.
Risperidone (Risperdal) key warnings and precautions:

NMS: if suspected, immediately discontinue RISPERDAL and provide symptomatic treatment and monitoring. Tardive dyskinesia: potentially irreversible involuntary dyskinetic movements; consider discontinuation if signs appear. Metabolic changes (hyperglycemia, dyslipidemia, body weight gain) may ↑ cardiovascular/cerebrovascular risk. At-risk pts: fasting blood glucose testing at the beginning of and periodically during tx. Elevates prolactin levels; elevation persists during chronic administration. Consider monitoring orthostatic vital signs in pts for whom this is of concern. Leukopenia/neutropenia: pts w Hx of clinically significant low WBC — monitor CBC frequently during first few months; discontinue if clinically significant decline. May impair judgment, thinking, or motor skills — caution w operating hazardous machinery incl automobiles.
Risperidone (Risperdal) CI and interactions:

CI: known hypersensitivity to risperidone, paliperidone, or excipients. CYP2D6 inhibitors (fluoxetine, paroxetine) ↑ risperidone levels — reduce initial dose; do not exceed 8 mg/day. Enzyme inducers (carbamazepine) ↓ risperidone levels — ↑ dose up to double the usual dose; titrate slowly. May antagonize the effects of levodopa and dopamine agonists.
Olanzapine (Zyprexa) boxed warning:
Boxed: elderly pts w dementia-related psychosis on antipsychotics at ↑ risk of death; ZYPREXA not approved for dementia-related psychosis.
Olanzapine (Zyprexa) elderly dementia risk:
Cerebrovascular adverse events (stroke, TIA), incl fatalities, in elderly pts w dementia-related psychosis.
Olanzapine (Zyprexa) key warnings and precautions:

NMS: manage w immediate discontinuation and close monitoring. DRESS reported w olanzapine (rash/exfoliative dermatitis, eosinophilia, fever, lymphadenopathy w hepatitis, nephritis, pneumonitis, myocarditis, pericarditis); sometimes fatal — discontinue if suspected. Metabolic changes incl hyperglycemia, dyslipidemia, weight gain may be associated w ↑ cardiovascular/cerebrovascular risk. Monitor fasting blood glucose and lipid profile at the beginning of and periodically during tx. Tardive dyskinesia: potentially irreversible involuntary dyskinetic movements; consider discontinuing if signs appear. May induce orthostatic hypotension w dizziness, tachycardia, bradycardia, and in some pts syncope, esp during initial dose titration. ⍉ concomitant IM olanzapine and parenteral benzodiazepine — potential for excessive sedation and cardiorespiratory depression. Leukopenia/neutropenia/agranulocytosis: pts w Hx of clinically significant low WBC — monitor CBC frequently during first few months; discontinue if clinically significant decline. Elevates prolactin levels, and the elevation persists during chronic administration. Use w caution w other anticholinergic drugs and in pts w urinary retention, prostatic hypertrophy, constipation, paralytic ileus.
Olanzapine (Zyprexa) interactions:
Diazepam & alcohol may potentiate orthostatic hypotension; carbamazepine ↑ olanzapine clearance; fluvoxamine may ↑ olanzapine levels.
Clozapine (Clozaril) boxed warning:
Boxed: severe neutropenia w ↑ risk of serious and potentially fatal infections.
Clozapine (Clozaril) ANC monitoring:
Obtain baseline ANC b4 initiation; not recommended if baseline ANC <1500/μL; monitor ANC regularly throughout tx. Benign Ethnic Neutropenia: initiation not recommended if ANC <1000/μL.
Clozapine (Clozaril) cardiovascular warnings:

Orthostatic hypotension, bradycardia, syncope, cardiac arrest — risk highest during initial titration, esp w rapid escalation; can occur w first dose, at doses as low as 12.5 mg/day, or on restart after even brief interruption; start 12.5 mg once or twice daily, titrate slowly, use divided doses. Fatal myocarditis/cardiomyopathy: discontinue and obtain cardiac evaluation on suspicion; generally do not rechallenge. Myocarditis/pericarditis most frequently within first 2 months; cardiomyopathy symptoms usually after 8 weeks.
Clozapine (Clozaril) seizures, dementia mortality, GI and QT:

Seizures are dose-related; initiate low dose (12.5 mg), titrate slowly, use divided dosing. Elderly pts w dementia-related psychosis on antipsychotics at ↑ risk of death; CLOZARIL not approved for dementia-related psychosis. GI hypomotility: if constipation identified, monitor closely and treat promptly w laxatives; consider prophylactic laxatives in high-risk pts. Discontinue CLOZARIL if QTc exceeds 500 msec.
Clozapine (Clozaril) NMS, interactions, overdose:

NMS: immediately discontinue and monitor closely. Reduce CLOZARIL dose to one-third w strong CYP1A2 inhibitors (fluvoxamine, ciprofloxacin, enoxacin). OD: sedation, delirium, coma, tachycardia, hypotension, respiratory depression/failure, hypersalivation; fatal overdoses generally above 2500 mg. No specific antidote; establish/maintain airway, ensure oxygenation and ventilation, monitor cardiac status and vital signs.
